sentences.zh: 起昭陽協洽，盡閼逢敦牂，凡十二年。

translations.literal: From Zhaoyang Xiehe through Efeng Dunjiang; twelve years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhaoyang Xiehe through Efeng Dunjiang—twelve years in all.

sentences.zh: 世宗孝武皇帝下之下 天漢三年（癸未，公元前九八年） 1 春，二月，王卿有罪自殺，以執金吾杜周為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Shizong Emperor Xiaowu, Lower Part Two. Tianhan year 3 (guiwei, 98 BCE). 1. In spring, the second month, Wang Qing, guilty of a crime, killed himself; Commandant of the Capital Guard Du Zhou was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong Emperor Xiaowu, Lower Part Two. Tianhan year 3 (guiwei, 98 BCE). 1. In spring, the second month, Wang Qing, found guilty of a crime, killed himself; Commandant of the Capital Guard Du Zhou was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: ---- 2 初榷酒酤。

translations.literal: ----2 For the first time wine was monopolized for franchised sale.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 For the first time the state monopolized wine for franchised sale.

sentences.zh: ---- 3 三月，上行幸泰山，脩封，祀明堂，因受計。

translations.literal: ----3 In the third month, the emperor traveled in favor to Mount Tai, performed the feng, sacrificed at the Bright Hall, and thereupon received the annual accounts.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the third month, the emperor traveled to Mount Tai, performed the feng, sacrificed at the Bright Hall, and thereupon received the annual accounts.

sentences.zh: 還，祠常山，瘞玄玉。

translations.literal: On returning, he sacrificed at Mount Chang and buried dark jade.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he sacrificed at Mount Chang and buried dark jade.

sentences.zh: 方士之候祠神人、入海求蓬萊者終無有驗，而公孫卿猶以大人跡為解。

translations.literal: The masters of the methods who awaited spirit-men at sacrifices and those who entered the sea seeking Penglai in the end had no verification, yet Gongsun Qing still explained it by the footprints of a great man.
translations.idiomatic: The masters of the methods who awaited spirit-men at sacrifices and those who entered the sea seeking Penglai never obtained proof, yet Gongsun Qing still explained it away with the footprints of a great man.

sentences.zh: 天子益怠厭方士之怪迂語矣，然猶羈縻不絕，冀遇其真。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven grew ever more slack and weary of the masters' strange and perverse talk, yet still kept them tethered without cutting them off, hoping to encounter a true one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew ever more weary of the masters' strange and perverse talk, yet still kept them tethered without cutting them off, hoping to encounter a true one.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，方士言神祠者彌眾，然其效可睹矣。

translations.literal: From this time onward, masters of the methods who spoke of spirit worship grew ever more numerous, yet their effects could be seen.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward, masters who spoke of spirit worship grew ever more numerous, yet their effects were plain to see.

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, there was great drought.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, there was great drought.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: An amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ---- 5 秋，匈奴入雁門。

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, the Xiongnu entered Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, the Xiongnu entered Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 太守坐畏愞棄市。

translations.literal: The governor, convicted of cowardice and slackness, was abandoned in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The governor, convicted of cowardice and slackness, was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: ---- 天漢四年（甲申，公元前九七年） 1 春，正月，朝諸侯王於甘泉宮。

translations.literal: ----Tianhan year 4 (jiashen, 97 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, the feudal kings were received in audience at Ganquan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: ----Tianhan year 4 (jiashen, 97 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, the feudal kings were received in audience at Ganquan Palace.

sentences.zh: ---- 2 發天下七科謫及勇敢士，遣貳師將軍李廣利將騎六萬、步兵七萬出朔方；

translations.literal: ----2 Troops were raised from all under Heaven among the seven categories of banishment and brave men; Ershi General Li Guangli was sent leading sixty thousand cavalry and seventy thousand infantry out from Shuofang;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Troops were raised from across the realm among the seven categories of banishment and brave men; Ershi General Li Guangli was sent with sixty thousand cavalry and seventy thousand infantry out from Shuofang;

sentences.zh: 強弩都尉路博德將萬餘人與貳師會；

translations.literal: Strong Crossbow Commandant Lu Bode led more than ten thousand men to join Ershi;
translations.idiomatic: Strong Crossbow Commandant Lu Bode led more than ten thousand men to join Ershi;

sentences.zh: 游擊將軍韓說將步兵三萬人出五原；

translations.literal: Mobile Strike General Han Yue led thirty thousand infantry out from Wuyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Strike General Han Yue led thirty thousand infantry out from Wuyuan;

sentences.zh: 因杅將軍公孫敖將騎萬、步兵三萬人出雁門。

translations.literal: Yin'yu General Gongsun Ao led ten thousand cavalry and thirty thousand infantry out from Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin'yu General Gongsun Ao led ten thousand cavalry and thirty thousand infantry out from Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 匈奴聞之，悉遠其累重於余吾水北；

translations.literal: The Xiongnu heard of it and all moved their baggage far to the north of the Yuwu River;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu heard of it and moved all their baggage far north of the Yuwu River;

sentences.zh: 而單于以兵十萬待水南，與貳師接戰。

translations.literal: the chanyu with a hundred thousand troops waited south of the water and engaged Ershi in battle.
translations.idiomatic: the chanyu with a hundred thousand troops waited south of the river and engaged Ershi in battle.

sentences.zh: 貳師解而引歸，與單于連鬥十餘日。

translations.literal: Ershi disengaged and withdrew, fighting the chanyu in succession for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Ershi disengaged and withdrew, fighting the chanyu in succession for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 游擊無所得。

translations.literal: Mobile Strike gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Strike gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 因杅與左賢王戰，不利，引歸。

translations.literal: Yin'yu fought the Left Worthy King, did not prevail, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yin'yu fought the Left Worthy King, did not prevail, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時上遣敖深入匈奴迎李陵，敖軍無功還，因曰：「捕得生口，言李陵教單于為兵以備漢軍，故臣無所得。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had sent Ao deep into the Xiongnu to welcome Li Ling; Ao's army returned without achievement and thereupon said: "We captured a live captive who said Li Ling taught the chanyu to array troops against the Han army, and therefore your subject gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had sent Ao deep into the Xiongnu to welcome Li Ling; Ao's army returned without success and reported, "We captured a live captive who said Li Ling taught the chanyu to array troops against the Han army, and therefore your subject gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 」上於是族陵家。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon exterminated Ling's clan.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon exterminated Ling's clan.

sentences.zh: 既而聞之，乃漢將降匈奴者李緒，非陵也。

translations.literal: Soon afterward it was heard that it was Li Xu, a Han general who had surrendered to the Xiongnu, and not Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward it was learned that it was Li Xu, a Han general who had surrendered to the Xiongnu, and not Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵使人刺殺緒。

translations.literal: Ling sent men to stab and kill Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Ling sent men to stab and kill Xu.

sentences.zh: 大閼氏欲殺陵，單于匿之北方。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort wished to kill Ling; the chanyu hid him in the north.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Consort wished to kill Ling; the chanyu hid him in the north.

sentences.zh: 大閼氏死，乃還。

translations.literal: When the Grand Consort died, he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Consort died, he returned.

sentences.zh: 單于以女妻陵，立為右校王，與衛律皆貴用事。

translations.literal: The chanyu gave his daughter in marriage to Ling and established him as Right Commandant King; he and Wei Lü were both honored and held power.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu gave his daughter to Ling in marriage and made him Right Commandant King; he and Wei Lü were both honored and held power.

sentences.zh: 衛律常在單于左右；

translations.literal: Wei Lü was constantly at the chanyu's side;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lü was constantly at the chanyu's side;

sentences.zh: 陵居外，有大事乃入議。

translations.literal: Ling dwelt outside; only when there was a great affair did he enter to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Ling lived apart; only when a great affair arose did he enter to deliberate.

sentences.zh: ---- 3 夏，四月，立皇子髆為昌邑王。

translations.literal: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, the emperor's son Bo was established as King of Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, the emperor's son Bo was established as King of Changyi.

sentences.zh: ---- 太始元年（乙酉，公元前九六年） 1 春，正月，公孫敖坐妻為巫蠱要斬。

translations.literal: ----Taishi year 1 (yiyou, 96 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, Gongsun Ao, convicted because his wife practiced witchcraft, was beheaded at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: ----Taishi year 1 (yiyou, 96 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, Gongsun Ao, convicted because his wife practiced witchcraft, was beheaded at the waist.

sentences.zh: ---- 2 徙郡國豪桀於茂陵。

translations.literal: ----2 Powerful and prominent men of the commanderies and kingdoms were moved to Maoling.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Powerful and prominent men of the commanderies and kingdoms were moved to Maoling.

sentences.zh: ---- 3 夏，六月，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----3 In summer, the sixth month, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the sixth month, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ---- 4 是歲，匈奴且鞮侯單于死。

translations.literal: ----4 That year, the Xiongnu chanyu Qiedi Hou died.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 That year the Xiongnu chanyu Qiedi Hou died.

sentences.zh: 有兩子，長為左賢王，次為左大將。

translations.literal: He had two sons: the elder was Left Worthy King, the younger Left Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder was Left Worthy King, the younger Left Grand General.

sentences.zh: 左賢王未至，貴人以為有病，更立左大將為單于。

translations.literal: The Left Worthy King had not arrived; the nobles thought him ill and instead established the Left Grand General as chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Worthy King had not arrived; the nobles thought him ill and instead made the Left Grand General chanyu.

sentences.zh: 左賢王聞之，不敢進。

translations.literal: The Left Worthy King heard of it and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Worthy King heard of it and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 左大將使人召左賢王而讓位焉。

translations.literal: The Left Grand General sent men to summon the Left Worthy King and yield the throne to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Grand General sent men to summon the Left Worthy King and yield the throne to him.

sentences.zh: 左賢王辭以病，左大將不聽，謂曰：「即不幸死，傳之於我。

translations.literal: The Left Worthy King declined on grounds of illness; the Left Grand General would not listen and said to him: "If you should unhappily die, pass it to me.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Worthy King declined on grounds of illness; the Left Grand General would not listen and said, "If you should die, pass the throne to me.

sentences.zh: 」左賢王許之，遂立，為狐鹿姑單于。

translations.literal: " The Left Worthy King assented; he was thereupon established as chanyu, titled Hulu Gu.
translations.idiomatic: " The Left Worthy King assented; he was thereupon established as chanyu, titled Hulu Gu.

sentences.zh: 以左大將為左賢王，數年，病死；

translations.literal: The Left Grand General was made Left Worthy King; after several years he died of illness;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Grand General was made Left Worthy King; after several years he died of illness;

sentences.zh: 其子先賢撣不得代，更以為日逐王。

translations.literal: his son Xianxian Shan could not succeed him and was instead made Riyu King.
translations.idiomatic: his son Xianxian Shan could not succeed him and was instead made Riyu King.

sentences.zh: 單于自以其子為左賢王。

translations.literal: The chanyu himself made his own son Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu himself made his own son Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: ---- 太始二年（丙戌，公元前九五年） 1 春，正月，上行幸回中。

translations.literal: ----Taishi year 2 (bingxu, 95 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled in favor to Huizhong.
translations.idiomatic: ----Taishi year 2 (bingxu, 95 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled to Huizhong.

sentences.zh: ---- 2 杜周卒，光祿大夫暴勝之為御史大夫。

translations.literal: ----2 Du Zhou died; Palace Grandee Bao Shengzhi was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Du Zhou died; Palace Grandee Bao Shengzhi was made Censor-in-Chief.

translations.literal: ----3 In autumn, there was drought.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In autumn, there was drought.

sentences.zh: ---- 4 趙中大夫白公奏穿渠引涇水，首起谷口，尾入櫟陽，注渭中，袤二百里，溉田四千五百餘頃，因名曰白渠；

translations.literal: ----4 Zhao Palace Grandee Bai Gong memorialized to cut a canal and draw the Jing River, beginning at Gukou and ending at Liyang, pouring into the Wei—two hundred li in length, irrigating more than forty-five hundred qing of fields; it was therefore named the Bai Canal;
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Zhao Palace Grandee Bai Gong memorialized to cut a canal drawing the Jing River from Gukou to Liyang, pouring into the Wei—two hundred li long, irrigating more than forty-five hundred qing of fields; it was therefore named the Bai Canal;

sentences.zh: 民得其饒。

translations.literal: the people gained its abundance.
translations.idiomatic: the people gained its abundance.

sentences.zh: ---- 太始三年（丁亥，公元前九四年） 1 春，正月，上行幸甘泉宮。

translations.literal: ----Taishi year 3 (dinghai, 94 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled in favor to Ganquan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: ----Taishi year 3 (dinghai, 94 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled to Ganquan Palace.

sentences.zh: 二月，幸東海，獲赤雁。

translations.literal: In the second month, he favored Donghai and obtained a red wild goose.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, he visited Donghai and obtained a red wild goose.

sentences.zh: 幸琅邪，禮日成山，登之罘，浮大海而還。

translations.literal: He favored Langye, performed rites at Mount Richeng, ascended Mount Zhi, floated upon the great sea, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Langye, performed rites at Mount Richeng, ascended Mount Zhi, sailed upon the great sea, and returned.

sentences.zh: ---- 2 是歲，皇子弗陵生。

translations.literal: ----2 That year, the imperial son Fuling was born.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 That year the imperial son Fuling was born.

sentences.zh: 弗陵母曰河間趙倢伃，居鉤弋宮，任身十四月而生。

translations.literal: Fuling's mother was Lady Jieyi Zhao of Hejian, dwelling in Gouyi Palace; she carried the child fourteen months before giving birth.
translations.idiomatic: Fuling's mother was Lady Jieyi Zhao of Hejian, dwelling in Gouyi Palace; she carried the child fourteen months before giving birth.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「聞昔堯十四月而生，今鉤弋亦然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have heard that in former times Yao was born after fourteen months; now Gouyi is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have heard that in former times Yao was born after fourteen months; now Gouyi is likewise.

sentences.zh: 」乃命其所生門曰堯母門。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered the gate where she gave birth called Gate of Yao's Mother.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon named the gate where she gave birth Gate of Yao's Mother.

sentences.zh: :臣光曰：為人君者，動靜舉措不可不慎，發於中必形於外，天下無不知之。

translations.literal: : Your subject Guang says: As a ruler, movement and rest, every act and step cannot but be cautious; what arises within must take form without, and all under Heaven will know it.
translations.idiomatic: : Your subject Guang says: As a ruler, every movement and every act cannot but be cautious; what arises within must take form without, and all under Heaven will know it.

sentences.zh: 當是時也，皇后、太子皆無恙，而命鉤弋之門曰堯母，非名也。

translations.literal: At that time the empress and crown prince were both unharmed, yet he named Gouyi's gate Yao's Mother—this was not a proper name.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empress and crown prince were both unharmed, yet he named Gouyi's gate Yao's Mother—this was not a proper name.

sentences.zh: 是以奸人逆探上意，知其奇愛少子，欲以為嗣，遂有危皇后、太子之心，卒成巫蠱之禍，悲夫！

translations.literal: For this reason wicked men probed the emperor's intent in reverse, knew he singularly loved the younger son and wished to make him heir, and thereupon harbored thoughts of endangering the empress and crown prince, until at last the witchcraft calamity was completed—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: For this reason wicked men probed the emperor's intent in reverse, knew he singularly loved the younger son and wished to make him heir, and harbored thoughts of endangering the empress and crown prince, until at last the witchcraft calamity was completed—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: ---- 3 趙人江充為水衡都尉。

translations.literal: ----3 The Zhao man Jiang Chong was made Chief Steward for Water and Parks.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 The Zhao man Jiang Chong was made Chief Steward for Water and Parks.

sentences.zh: 初，充為趙敬肅王客，得罪於太子丹，亡逃；

translations.literal: At the outset, Chong had been a retainer of King Jingsu of Zhao, offended the heir Dan, and fled as a fugitive;
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Chong had been a retainer of King Jingsu of Zhao, offended the heir Dan, and fled;

sentences.zh: 詣闕告趙太子陰事，太子坐廢。

translations.literal: he came to the palace gates to report the Zhao heir's secret affairs, and the heir was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: he came to the palace gates to report the Zhao heir's secret affairs, and the heir was deposed.

sentences.zh: 上召充入見。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Chong to enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Chong to audience.

sentences.zh: 充容貌魁岸，被服輕靡，上奇之；

translations.literal: Chong's appearance was lofty and imposing, his dress light and extravagant; the emperor marveled at him;
translations.idiomatic: Chong's appearance was lofty and imposing, his dress light and extravagant; the emperor marveled at him;

sentences.zh: 與語政事，大悅，由是有寵，拜為直指繡衣使者，使督察貴戚、近臣逾侈者。

translations.literal: in speaking with him of state affairs he was greatly pleased; thereby he gained favor and was appointed Straight-Pointing Embroidered-Robe Envoy, charged to oversee and inspect noble kin and close ministers who exceeded in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: in speaking with him of state affairs he was greatly pleased; thereby he gained favor and was appointed Straight-Pointing Embroidered-Robe Envoy, charged to inspect noble kin and close ministers who exceeded in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 充舉劾無所避，上以為忠直，所言皆中意。

translations.literal: Chong impeached without avoiding anyone; the emperor considered him loyal and upright, and everything he said hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Chong impeached without avoiding anyone; the emperor considered him loyal and upright, and everything he said hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 嘗從上甘泉，逢太子家使乘車馬行馳道中，充以屬吏。

translations.literal: Once, following the emperor to Ganquan, he encountered the crown prince's household envoy driving a carriage and horses along the imperial speedway; Chong handed him over to the attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: Once, following the emperor to Ganquan, he encountered the crown prince's household envoy driving along the imperial speedway; Chong handed him over to the attending officials.

sentences.zh: 太子聞之，使人謝充曰：「非愛車馬，誠不欲令上聞之，以教敕亡素者，唯江君寬之。

translations.literal: The crown prince heard of it and sent men to apologize to Chong, saying: "It is not that I love the carriage and horses; I truly did not wish to let the emperor hear of it, lest he admonish my lack of discipline—only let Lord Jiang be lenient.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince heard of it and sent men to apologize to Chong, saying, "It is not that I love the carriage and horses; I truly did not wish the emperor to hear of it, lest he admonish my lack of discipline—only let Lord Jiang be lenient.

sentences.zh: 」充不聽，遂白奏，上曰：「人臣當如是矣！

translations.literal: " Chong would not listen and thereupon reported in memorial; the emperor said: "A minister ought to be like this!
translations.idiomatic: " Chong would not listen and reported in memorial; the emperor said, "A minister ought to be like this!

sentences.zh: 」大見信用，威震京師。

translations.literal: " He was greatly trusted and his authority shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " He was greatly trusted and his authority shook the capital.

sentences.zh: ---- 太始四年（戊子，公元前九三年） 1 春，三月，上行幸泰山。

translations.literal: ----Taishi year 4 (wuzi, 93 BCE). 1. In spring, the third month, the emperor traveled in favor to Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: ----Taishi year 4 (wuzi, 93 BCE). 1. In spring, the third month, the emperor traveled to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 壬午，祀高祖於明堂以配上帝，因受計。

translations.literal: On renwu, he sacrificed to High Ancestor at the Bright Hall to accompany the High God, and thereupon received the accounts.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he sacrificed to High Ancestor at the Bright Hall to accompany the High God, and thereupon received the accounts.

sentences.zh: 癸未，祀孝景皇帝於明堂。

translations.literal: On guiwei, he sacrificed to Emperor Xiaojing at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he sacrificed to Emperor Xiaojing at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 甲申，修封。

translations.literal: On jiashen, he performed the feng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he performed the feng.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，禪石閭。

translations.literal: On bingxu, he performed the shan at Stone Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he performed the shan at Stone Lodge.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，幸不其。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, he favored Buqi.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, he visited Buqi.

sentences.zh: 五月，還，幸建章宮，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on returning, he favored Jianzhang Palace and proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on his return, he visited Jianzhang Palace and proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ---- 2 冬，十月，甲寅晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----2 In winter, the tenth month, on the last day of the month jiayin, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In winter, the tenth month, on the last day of the month jiayin, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: ---- 3 十二月，上行幸雍，祠五畤。

translations.literal: ----3 In the twelfth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the twelfth month, the emperor traveled to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.

sentences.zh: 西至安定、北地。

translations.literal: He went west to Anding and Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: He went west to Anding and Beidi.

sentences.zh: 征和元年（己丑，公元前九二年） 1 春，正月，上還，幸建章宮。

translations.literal: Zhenghe year 1 (jichou, 92 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, the emperor returned and favored Jianzhang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe year 1 (jichou, 92 BCE). 1. In spring, the first month, the emperor returned and visited Jianzhang Palace.

translations.idiomatic: At that time Nao Ji's elder brother was a Han eunuch; the emperor summoned him and asked, "What of the Nao lad?

translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Many desires do not suit ruling a state and governing the people.

translations.literal: " He asked Marquis of Wushi Chang, who said: "Neither fault nor praise.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked Marquis of Wushi Chang, who said, "Neither fault nor praise.

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Such as this will do.

translations.idiomatic: The man cast aside his sword and fled; they pursued him but did not capture him.

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and beheaded the gate warden.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and beheaded the gate warden.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，發三輔騎士大搜上林，閉長安城門索；

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, he raised knights of the Three Metropolises for a great search of Shanglin and closed the Chang'an city gates to hunt;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, he raised knights of the Three Metropolises for a great search of Shanglin and closed the Chang'an city gates to hunt;

translations.literal: only after eleven days was the lock lifted.

translations.idiomatic: ----5 Chancellor Gongsun He's wife Junru was Empress Wei's elder sister; He thereby gained favor.

sentences.zh: 賀子敬聲代父為太僕，驕奢不奉法，擅用北軍錢千九百萬；

translations.literal: He's son Jingsheng succeeded his father as Grand Master of the Household, was arrogant and extravagant and did not observe the law, and on his own authority used nineteen million of Northern Army funds;
translations.idiomatic: He's son Jingsheng succeeded his father as Grand Master of the Household, was arrogant and extravagant and did not observe the law, and on his own authority used nineteen million of Northern Army funds;

translations.literal: when discovered, he was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: when discovered, he was cast into prison.

translations.literal: At this time an edict urgently sought to capture the Yangling great hero Zhu Anshi; He volunteered to pursue and capture Anshi to redeem Jingsheng's crime; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: At this time an edict urgently sought the Yangling great hero Zhu Anshi; He volunteered to pursue and capture Anshi to redeem Jingsheng's crime, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 後果得安世。

translations.literal: Later they indeed obtained Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Later they indeed captured Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安世笑曰：「丞相禍及宗矣！

translations.literal: Anshi laughed and said: "The Chancellor's calamity will reach his clan!
translations.idiomatic: Anshi laughed and said, "The Chancellor's calamity will reach his clan!

sentences.zh: 」遂從獄中上書，告「敬聲與陽石公主私通；

translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon from prison he memorialized, accusing Jingsheng of illicit relations with the Yangshi Princess;

translations.idiomatic: when the emperor would go to Ganquan, had witches bury doll figures on the imperial carriage road and curse the emperor with evil words.

translations.idiomatic: " ---- Zhenghe year 2 (Gengyin, 91 BCE) 1 In spring, the first month, He was imprisoned and investigated;

sentences.zh: 父子死獄中，家族。

translations.literal: Father and son died in prison; the clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son died in prison, and the clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 以涿郡太守劉屈氂為左丞相，封澎侯。

translations.literal: Liu Quji, Governor of Zhuo commandery, was made Left Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quji, Governor of Zhuo commandery, was made Left Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Peng.

sentences.zh: 屈氂，中山靖王子也。

translations.literal: Quji was a son of King Jing of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Quji was a son of King Jing of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: ---- 2 夏，四月，大風，發屋折木。

translations.literal: ---- 2 In summer, the fourth month, great wind tore houses open and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 2 In summer, the fourth month, a great wind tore houses open and broke trees.

sentences.zh: ---- 3 閏月，諸邑公主、陽石公主及皇后弟子長平侯伉皆坐巫蠱誅。

translations.literal: ---- 3 In the intercalary month, the Princess of Zhuyi, the Yangshi Princess, and the empress's nephew Marquis of Changping Kang were all executed for witchcraft.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 3 In the intercalary month, the Princess of Zhuyi, the Yangshi Princess, and the empress's nephew Marquis of Changping Kang were all executed for witchcraft.

sentences.zh: ---- 4 上行幸甘泉。

translations.idiomatic: ---- 4 The emperor traveled to Ganquan.
