translations.literal: ---- 5 At first, the emperor was twenty-nine when he bore the Aloof Crown Prince and greatly loved him.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 5 At first the emperor was twenty-nine when the Aloof Crown Prince was born, and he greatly loved him.

sentences.zh: 及長，性仁恕溫謹，上嫌其材能少，不類己；

translations.literal: When he grew up, his nature was benevolent, forgiving, warm, and cautious; the emperor disliked that his talent and ability were few and unlike himself;
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was benevolent, forgiving, warm, and cautious; the emperor disliked his limited talent and ability, finding him unlike himself;

sentences.zh: 而所幸王夫人生子閎，李姬生子旦、胥，李夫人生子髆，皇后、太子寵浸衰，常有不自安之意。

translations.literal: while the Wang lady he favored bore Hong, Lady Li bore Dan and Xu, Lady Li bore Bo; the empress and crown prince's favor gradually declined, and they often had feelings of not being at ease.
translations.idiomatic: while the Wang lady he favored bore Hong, Lady Li bore Dan and Xu, and Lady Li bore Bo; favor toward the empress and crown prince gradually declined, and they often felt ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 上覺之，謂大將軍青曰：「漢家庶事草創，加四夷侵陵中國，朕不變更制度，後世無法；

translations.literal: The emperor noticed and said to Grand General Qing: "The Han house's many affairs are still in the founding stage, plus the four barbarians invade and harass China—if I do not change and renew institutions, later generations will have no models;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed and said to Grand General Qing, "The Han house's many affairs are still in the founding stage, and the four barbarians invade and harass China—if I do not change and renew institutions, later generations will have no models;

sentences.zh: 不出師征伐，天下不安；

translations.literal: if I do not send troops out to campaign and attack, all under Heaven will not be secure;
translations.idiomatic: if I do not send troops out to campaign, all under Heaven will not be secure;

sentences.zh: 為此者不得不勞民。

translations.literal: for this one cannot but burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: for this one cannot but burden the people.

sentences.zh: 若後世又如朕所為，是襲亡秦之跡也。

translations.literal: If later generations again do as I do, that is following the traces of the perished Qin.
translations.idiomatic: If later generations again do as I do, that is following the path of the perished Qin.

sentences.zh: 太子敦重好靜，必能安天下，不使朕憂。

translations.literal: The crown prince is staunch and grave and loves quiet—he will surely be able to secure all under Heaven and not make me worry.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is staunch and grave and loves quiet—he will surely secure all under Heaven and spare me worry.

sentences.zh: 欲求守文之主，安有賢於太子者乎！

translations.literal: Wishing to seek a ruler who guards the written statutes, is there anyone more worthy than the crown prince!
translations.idiomatic: If one seeks a ruler who guards the written statutes, who is more worthy than the crown prince!

sentences.zh: 聞皇后與太子有不安之意，豈有之邪？

translations.literal: I have heard the empress and crown prince have feelings of unease—could there really be such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the empress and crown prince feel uneasy—could that really be so?

sentences.zh: 可以意曉之。

translations.literal: You may convey my meaning to make them understand.
translations.idiomatic: You may convey my meaning to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 」大將軍頓首謝。

translations.literal: " The Grand General bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand General bowed his head in thanks.

sentences.zh: 皇后聞之，脫簪請罪。

translations.literal: The empress heard and removed her hairpin to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The empress heard and removed her hairpin to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 太子每諫證伐四夷，上笑曰：「吾當其勞，以逸遺汝，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: The crown prince repeatedly remonstrated against campaigning against the four barbarians; the emperor laughed and said: "I will bear the labor and leave ease to pass on to you—is that not acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince repeatedly remonstrated against campaigning against the four barbarians; the emperor laughed and said, "I will bear the labor and leave ease for you—is that not acceptable!

sentences.zh: 」 上每行幸，常以後事付太子，宮內付皇后。

translations.literal: " Whenever the emperor traveled in favor, he often entrusted later affairs to the crown prince and matters within the palace to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever the emperor traveled, he often entrusted later affairs to the crown prince and palace matters to the empress.

sentences.zh: 有所平決，還，白其最，上亦無異，有時不省也。

translations.literal: When there were decisions made, on return they reported the main points; the emperor also had no objection—sometimes he did not examine them.
translations.idiomatic: When decisions were made, on return they reported the main points; the emperor raised no objection—sometimes he did not even look into them.

sentences.zh: 上用法嚴，多任深刻吏。

translations.literal: The emperor used law strictly and mostly employed severe, penetrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor applied the law strictly and mostly employed harsh, penetrating officials.

sentences.zh: 太子寬厚，多所平反，雖得百姓心，而用法大臣皆不悅。

translations.literal: The crown prince was generous and thick and often overturned wrongful verdicts; though he gained the people's hearts, the law-using great ministers were all displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was generous and often overturned wrongful verdicts; though he won the people's hearts, the ministers who applied the law were all displeased.

sentences.zh: 皇后恐久獲罪，每戒太子，宜留取上意，不應擅有所縱捨。

translations.literal: The empress feared long obtaining guilt and repeatedly warned the crown prince that he should keep to the emperor's intent and should not on his own have releases and pardons.
translations.idiomatic: The empress feared she would eventually be blamed and repeatedly warned the crown prince to keep to the emperor's intent and not on his own grant releases and pardons.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，是太子而非皇后。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and approved the crown prince but not the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and sided with the crown prince rather than the empress.

sentences.zh: 群臣寬厚長者皆附太子，而深酷用法者皆毀之。

translations.literal: Among the ministers, generous, thick elders all attached to the crown prince, while those who deeply and cruelly used law all slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Generous, senior ministers all attached to the crown prince, while those who applied the law harshly all slandered him.

sentences.zh: 邪臣多黨與，故太子譽少而毀多。

translations.literal: Wicked ministers mostly had factions, so the crown prince had little praise and much slander.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked ministers mostly had factions, so praise of the crown prince was scant and slander abundant.

sentences.zh: 衛青薨後，臣下無復外家為據，競欲構太子。

translations.literal: After Wei Qing died, the ministers below no longer had the maternal kin as reliance and competed to frame the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Qing died, the ministers no longer had the maternal kin as backing and competed to frame the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上與諸子疏，皇后希得見。

translations.literal: The emperor was distant from his sons; the empress rarely obtained audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was distant from his sons, and the empress rarely saw him.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗謁皇后，移日乃出。

translations.literal: The crown prince once called on the empress and only after a whole day came out.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince once called on the empress and did not emerge until a whole day had passed.

sentences.zh: 黃門蘇文告上曰：「太子與宮人戲。

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate Su Wen reported to the emperor: "The crown prince was sporting with palace women.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Gate Su Wen reported to the emperor, "The crown prince was sporting with palace women.

sentences.zh: 」上益太子宮人滿二百人。

translations.literal: " The emperor increased the crown prince's palace women to fill two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor increased the crown prince's palace women to two hundred.

sentences.zh: 太子後知之，心銜文。

translations.literal: The crown prince later learned and bore resentment in heart toward Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince later learned of it and bore resentment toward Wen.

sentences.zh: 文與小黃門常融、王弼等常微伺太子過，輒增加白之。

translations.literal: Wen with junior yellow gates Chang Rong, Wang Bi, and others constantly spied in secret for the crown prince's faults and whenever they found any added to their reports to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wen with junior yellow gates Chang Rong, Wang Bi, and others constantly spied on the crown prince's faults and reported every one they found.

sentences.zh: 皇后切齒，使太子白誅文等。

translations.literal: The empress gnashed her teeth and had the crown prince report to have Wen and the others executed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress gnashed her teeth and urged the crown prince to report and have Wen and the others executed.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「第勿為過，何畏文等！

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "Just do not commit faults—why fear Wen and the rest!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Just do not commit faults—why fear Wen and the rest!

sentences.zh: 上聰明，不信邪佞，不足憂也」上嘗小不平，使常融召太子，融言「太子有喜色」，上嘿然。

translations.literal: The emperor is intelligent and does not believe the wicked and flattering—there is insufficient cause for worry." The emperor was once slightly unwell and had Chang Rong summon the crown prince; Rong said "the crown prince had a pleased look"; the emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is intelligent and does not believe the wicked and flattering—there is no need to worry." The emperor was once slightly unwell and had Chang Rong summon the crown prince; Rong said the crown prince had a pleased look; the emperor was silent.

sentences.zh: 及太子至，上察其貌，有涕泣處，而佯語笑，上怪之；

translations.literal: When the crown prince arrived, the emperor observed his appearance—there were places of weeping tears yet he pretended cheerful talk and laughter; the emperor found it strange;
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince arrived, the emperor observed his appearance—there were traces of tears yet he pretended cheerful talk and laughter; the emperor found it strange;

sentences.zh: 更微問，知其情，乃誅融。

translations.literal: further questioning in secret, he learned his feelings, and thereupon executed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: questioning him further in secret, he learned the truth and executed Rong.

sentences.zh: 皇后亦善自防閒，避嫌疑，雖久無寵，尚被禮遇。

translations.literal: The empress also was good at guarding herself against suspicion and avoiding doubtful points; though long without favor, she still received courtesy treatment.
translations.idiomatic: The empress also guarded herself carefully against suspicion; though long without favor, she still received courteous treatment.

sentences.zh: 是時，方士及諸神巫多聚京師，率皆左道惑眾，變幻無所不為。

translations.literal: At this time, method masters and various spirit witches mostly gathered in the capital, generally all crooked ways deluding the masses, transforming and conjuring with nothing they would not do.
translations.idiomatic: At this time method masters and spirit witches mostly gathered in the capital, generally all crooked ways deluding the masses, conjuring anything they pleased.

sentences.zh: 女巫往來宮中，教美人度厄，每屋輒埋木人祭祀之。

translations.literal: Witches went back and forth within the palace, teaching the beauties to pass through calamity; in every room they would bury wooden figures to sacrifice to them.
translations.idiomatic: Witches went back and forth within the palace, teaching the beauties rites to pass through calamity; in every room they buried wooden figures for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 因妒忌恚詈，更相告訐，以為祝詛上，無道。

translations.literal: Because of jealousy they cursed in anger and repeatedly accused one another, taking it as cursing the emperor—great impiety.
translations.idiomatic: Because of jealousy they cursed in anger and repeatedly accused one another of cursing the emperor—great impiety.

sentences.zh: 上怒，所殺後宮延及大臣，死者數百人。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; those killed in the rear palaces extended to great ministers—those who died numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry; executions in the rear palaces extended to great ministers, and several hundred died.

sentences.zh: 上心既以為疑，嘗晝寢，夢木人數千持杖欲擊上，上驚寤，因是體不平，遂苦忽忽善忘。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart already harbored suspicion; he once slept by day and dreamed several thousand wooden figures holding staves wishing to strike the emperor; the emperor started awake in fright; because of this his body was unwell and he came to suffer restless forgetfulness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's heart already harbored suspicion; he once slept by day and dreamed several thousand wooden figures holding staves about to strike him; he started awake in fright; thereafter his health failed and he suffered restless forgetfulness.

sentences.zh: 江充自以與太子及衛氏有隙，見上年老，恐晏駕後為太子所誅，因是為奸，言上疾祟在巫蠱。

translations.literal: Jiang Chong, considering himself to have a rift with the crown prince and the Wei clan, saw the emperor was old and feared that after the emperor's death he would be executed by the crown prince; he therefore acted wickedly, saying the emperor's illness and malign influence lay in witchcraft.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chong, knowing he had a rift with the crown prince and the Wei clan, saw the emperor was old and feared execution after the emperor's death; he therefore acted wickedly, saying the emperor's illness stemmed from witchcraft.

sentences.zh: 於是上以充為使者，治巫蠱獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor made Chong an envoy to investigate the witchcraft case.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor made Chong an envoy to investigate the witchcraft case.

sentences.zh: 充將胡巫掘地求偶人，捕蠱及夜祠、視鬼，染污令有處，輒收捕驗治，燒鐵鉗灼，強服之。

translations.literal: Chong led Hu witches to dig earth seeking doll figures, captured sorcery and night sacrifices and spirit-viewing; where stained pollution could be placed they would arrest and verify and try, burning iron pincers to cauterize and forcing confession.
translations.idiomatic: Chong led Hu witches to dig earth seeking doll figures, captured sorcery, night sacrifices, and spirit-viewing; wherever tainted evidence could be planted they arrested and tried the accused, burning iron pincers to cauterize and forcing confession.

sentences.zh: 民轉相誣以巫蠱，吏輒劾以為大逆無道；

translations.literal: The people turned and accused one another of witchcraft; officials would impeach them as great treason without norm;
translations.idiomatic: The people turned and accused one another of witchcraft; officials would impeach them as great treason;

sentences.zh: 自京師、三輔連及郡、國，坐而死者前後數萬人。

translations.literal: from the capital, the three metropolitan areas, extending to commanderies and kingdoms—those who sat convicted and died before and after numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: from the capital and the three metropolitan areas to commanderies and kingdoms, those convicted and executed before and after numbered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 是時，上春秋高，疑左右皆為蠱祝詛；

translations.literal: At this time the emperor's years were advanced; he suspected those left and right all practiced sorcery and cursed;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor was advanced in years and suspected everyone around him of sorcery and cursing;

sentences.zh: 有與無，莫敢訟其冤者。

translations.literal: whether there was or was not, none dared argue their injustice.
translations.idiomatic: whether guilty or not, none dared plead their innocence.

sentences.zh: 充既知上意，因胡巫檀何言：「宮中有蠱氣，不除之，上終不差。

translations.literal: Chong having known the emperor's intent, had the Hu witch Tan He say: "Within the palace there is sorcery vapor; if not removed, the emperor will in the end not recover.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, knowing the emperor's intent, had the Hu witch Tan He say, "Within the palace there is sorcery vapor; if not removed, the emperor will never recover.

sentences.zh: 」上乃使充入宮，至省中，壞御座，掘地求蠱；

translations.literal: " The emperor then had Chong enter the palace, reaching the inner apartments, broke imperial seats, and dug earth seeking sorcery;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then had Chong enter the palace, reach the inner apartments, break imperial seats, and dig earth seeking sorcery;

sentences.zh: 又使按道侯韓說、御史章贛、黃門蘇文等助充。

translations.literal: and also had Marquis of Andao Han Shuo, censor Zhang Gan, Yellow Gate Su Wen, and others assist Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Marquis of Andao Han Shuo, Censor Zhang Gan, Yellow Gate Su Wen, and others assist Chong.

sentences.zh: 充先治後宮希幸夫人，以次及皇后、太子宮，掘地縱橫，太子、皇后無復施床處。

translations.literal: Chong first investigated the rear palace favored ladies, in order reaching the empress and crown prince's palace; digging earth crosswise and lengthwise, the crown prince and empress no longer had place to set beds.
translations.idiomatic: Chong first investigated favored ladies of the rear palace, then in turn the empress and crown prince's palaces; digging everywhere crosswise and lengthwise, the crown prince and empress no longer had room to set a bed.

sentences.zh: 充云：「於太子宮得木人尤多，又有帛書，所言不道；

translations.literal: Chong said: "In the crown prince's palace wooden figures obtained were especially many, and additionally there was silk writing; what was said was not according to the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "In the crown prince's palace especially many wooden figures were found, and additionally silk writing with impious words;

sentences.zh: 當奏聞。

translations.literal: it should be memorialized to inform.
translations.idiomatic: this should be memorialized to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」太子懼，問少傅石德。

translations.literal: " The crown prince was afraid and asked the Junior Tutor Shi De.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince was afraid and asked Junior Tutor Shi De.

sentences.zh: 德懼為師傅並誅，因謂太子曰：「前丞相父子、兩公主及衛氏皆坐此，今巫與使者掘地得征驗，不知巫置之邪，將實有也，無以自明。

translations.literal: De feared being executed together as tutor and therefore said to the crown prince: "Previously the chancellor father and son, two princesses, and the Wei clan all sat convicted for this; now the witches and envoy dig earth and obtain verifying evidence—we do not know whether the witches placed them or they really exist; there is no means to clarify oneself.
translations.idiomatic: De feared being executed with his pupil and therefore said to the crown prince, "Previously the chancellor father and son, two princesses, and the Wei clan were all convicted for this; now the witches and envoy dig earth and obtain evidence—we do not know whether the witches planted it or it really exists; there is no way to clear oneself.

sentences.zh: 可矯以節收捕充等繫獄，窮治其奸詐。

translations.literal: You may falsely use the staff of office to arrest Chong and the rest and imprison them in prison, exhaustively trying their wicked deception.
translations.idiomatic: You may falsely use the staff of office to arrest Chong and the rest, imprison them, and exhaustively try their wicked deception.

sentences.zh: 且上疾在甘泉，皇后及家吏請問皆不報；

translations.literal: Moreover the emperor's illness is at Ganquan; the empress and household officials' requests for news all go unanswered;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the emperor is ill at Ganquan; the empress and household officials' requests for news all go unanswered;

sentences.zh: 上存亡未可知，而奸臣如此，太子將不念秦扶蘇事邪？

translations.literal: the emperor's survival or death is not yet known, while wicked ministers are like this—will the crown prince not recall the matter of Qin's Fusu?
translations.idiomatic: the emperor's survival is unknown, while wicked ministers act like this—will the crown prince not recall what happened to Qin's Fusu?

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「吾人子，安得擅誅！

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "I am a man's son—how can I on my own authority execute!
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said, "I am a son—how can I execute on my own authority!

sentences.zh: 不如歸謝，幸得無罪。

translations.literal: Better to return and apologize, perhaps obtaining no guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Better to go and apologize and hope to escape guilt.

sentences.zh: 」太子將往之甘泉，而江充持太子甚急；

translations.literal: " The crown prince was about to go to Ganquan, but Jiang Chong pressed the crown prince very urgently;
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince was about to go to Ganquan, but Jiang Chong pressed him very urgently;

sentences.zh: 太子計不知所出，遂從石德計。

translations.literal: the crown prince's plans knew nowhere to go out; he thereupon followed Shi De's plan.
translations.idiomatic: the crown prince could think of no way out and thereupon followed Shi De's plan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬午，太子使客詐為使者，收捕充等。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renwu, the crown prince sent retainers falsely posing as envoys to arrest Chong and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renwu, the crown prince sent retainers posing as envoys to arrest Chong and the rest.

sentences.zh: 按道侯說疑使者有詐，不肯受詔，客格殺說。

translations.literal: Marquis of Andao Shuo suspected the envoys had deception and would not receive the edict; the retainers killed Shuo in struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Andao Shuo suspected the envoys were fraudulent and refused the edict; the retainers killed him in the struggle.

sentences.zh: 太子自臨斬充，罵曰：「趙虜！

translations.literal: The crown prince personally attended to behead Chong, cursing: "Zhao barbarian!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince personally beheaded Chong, cursing, "Zhao barbarian!

sentences.zh: 前亂乃國王父子不足邪！

translations.literal: Previously you disturbed the Zhao king father and son—not enough!
translations.idiomatic: Was it not enough that you before ruined the Zhao king and his son!

sentences.zh: 乃復亂吾父子也！

translations.literal: Now again you disturb our father and son!
translations.idiomatic: Now you come again to ruin our father and son!

sentences.zh: 」又炙胡巫上林中。

translations.literal: " He also roasted the Hu witch in Shanglin Park.
translations.idiomatic: " He also roasted the Hu witch in Shanglin Park.

sentences.zh: 太子使舍人無且持節夜入未央宮殿長秋門，因長御倚華具白皇后，發中廄車載射士，出武庫兵，發長樂宮衛卒。

translations.literal: The crown prince sent chamberlain Wunie holding the staff of office by night to enter Weiyang Palace's Eternal Autumn Gate; through chief attendant Yi Hua he fully informed the empress, issued central stable chariots carrying archers, brought out arsenal weapons, and mobilized Changle Palace guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince sent Chamberlain Wunie with the staff of office by night through Weiyang Palace's Eternal Autumn Gate; through Chief Attendant Yi Hua he fully informed the empress, mobilized central stable chariots with archers, brought out arsenal weapons, and raised Changle Palace guard troops.

sentences.zh: 長安擾亂，言太子反。

translations.literal: Chang'an was disturbed and chaotic; they said the crown prince had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an was thrown into turmoil; word spread that the crown prince had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 蘇文迸走，得亡歸甘泉，說太子無狀。

translations.literal: Su Wen burst away running and obtained escape back to Ganquan, reporting the crown prince's misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wen fled and escaped back to Ganquan, reporting the crown prince's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「太子必懼，又忿充等，故有此變。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The crown prince must be afraid and also angry at Chong and the rest—therefore there is this change.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The crown prince must be afraid and angry at Chong and the rest—hence this disturbance.

sentences.zh: 」乃使使召太子。

translations.literal: " He then sent an envoy to summon the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent an envoy to summon the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 使者不敢進，歸報云：「太子反已成，欲斬臣，臣逃歸。

translations.literal: The envoy did not dare advance and returned reporting: "The crown prince's rebellion is already accomplished; he wished to behead your servant; your servant fled back.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy did not dare advance and returned reporting, "The crown prince's rebellion is already accomplished; he wished to behead me, and I fled back.

sentences.zh: 」上大怒。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly angry.

sentences.zh: 丞相屈氂聞變，挺身逃，亡其印綬，使長史乘疾置以聞。

translations.literal: Chancellor Quji heard of the change, threw his body fleeing, lost his seal and cord, and had the chief clerk ride the express relay to report.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Quji heard of the disturbance, fled headlong, lost his seal and cord, and had the chief clerk ride the express relay to report.

sentences.zh: 上問：「丞相何為？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "What is the Chancellor doing?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What is the Chancellor doing?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「丞相秘之，未敢發兵。

translations.literal: " Reply: "The Chancellor is keeping it secret and does not dare send troops.
translations.idiomatic: " The reply was, "The Chancellor is keeping it secret and does not dare send troops.

sentences.zh: 」上怒曰：「事籍籍如此，何謂秘也！

translations.literal: " The emperor angrily said: "The affair is so widespread and noisy—what is called secret!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor angrily said, "The affair is so widespread—what do you mean by secret!

sentences.zh: 丞相無周公之風矣，周公不誅管、蔡乎！

translations.literal: The Chancellor lacks the Duke of Zhou's manner—did not the Duke of Zhou execute Guan and Cai!
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor lacks the Duke of Zhou's spirit—did not the Duke of Zhou execute Guan and Cai!

sentences.zh: 」乃賜丞相璽書曰：「捕斬反者，自有賞罰。

translations.literal: " He then bestowed on the Chancellor a sealed letter saying: "Capturing and beheading rebels—there are rewards and punishments of their own.
translations.idiomatic: " He then bestowed on the Chancellor a sealed letter saying, "Capturing and beheading rebels carry their own rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 以牛車為櫓，毋接短兵，多殺傷士眾！

translations.literal: Use oxcarts as shield-walls; do not engage with short weapons; do not greatly kill and wound officers and masses!
translations.idiomatic: Use oxcarts as shield-walls; do not engage at close quarters; do not greatly kill and wound troops!

sentences.zh: 堅閉城門，毋令反者得出！

translations.literal: Securely close the city gates; do not let rebels obtain exit!
translations.idiomatic: Securely close the city gates; do not let the rebels escape!

sentences.zh: 」太子宣言告令百官云：「帝在甘泉病困，疑有變；

translations.literal: " The crown prince proclaimed and instructed the hundred officials, saying: "The emperor is at Ganquan, ill and distressed, suspecting there is a change;
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince proclaimed to the hundred officials, "The emperor is at Ganquan, gravely ill, and suspects a coup;

sentences.zh: 奸臣欲作亂。

translations.literal: wicked ministers wish to make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: wicked ministers wish to rebel.

sentences.zh: 」上於是從甘泉來，幸城西建章宮，詔發三輔近縣兵，部中二千石以下，丞相兼將之。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon came from Ganquan, favored Jianzhang Palace west of the city, ordered mobilization of the three metropolitan areas' nearby counties' troops, those in departments and below two-thousand-dan, the Chancellor jointly commanding them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon came from Ganquan to Jianzhang Palace west of the city, ordered troops mobilized from nearby counties of the three metropolitan areas, and had the Chancellor jointly command all officials in departments and below two-thousand-dan.

sentences.zh: 太子亦遣使者矯制赦長安中都官囚徒，命少傅石德及賓客張光等分將；

translations.literal: The crown prince also sent envoys falsely using imperial orders to pardon Chang'an central capital officials' prisoners, ordered Junior Tutor Shi De and retainer Zhang Guang and others to divide command;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince also sent envoys with forged orders to pardon Chang'an prisoners held by central capital officials, and ordered Junior Tutor Shi De and retainer Zhang Guang and others to divide command;

sentences.zh: 使長安囚如侯持節發長水及宣曲胡騎，皆以裝會。

translations.literal: had Chang'an prisoner Ru Hou holding the staff of office mobilize Changshui and Xuqu Hu cavalry—all to assemble fully equipped.
translations.idiomatic: and had Chang'an prisoner Ru Hou, holding the staff of office, mobilize Changshui and Xuqu Hu cavalry, all to assemble fully equipped.

sentences.zh: 侍郎馬通使長安，因追捕如侯，告胡人曰：「節有詐，勿聽也！

translations.literal: Vice Minister Ma Tong was sent to Chang'an; pursuing Ru Hou along the way, he told the Hu: "The staff is deceptive—do not obey it!
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Ma Tong was sent to Chang'an; pursuing Ru Hou along the way, he told the Hu, "The staff is deceptive—do not obey it!

sentences.zh: 」遂斬如侯，引騎入長安；

translations.literal: " Thereupon he beheaded Ru Hou and led horsemen into Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he beheaded Ru Hou and led horsemen into Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 又發楫棹士以予大鴻臚商丘成。

translations.literal: He also sent boatmen and oarsmen to give to Grand Steward Shangqiu Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent boatmen and oarsmen to Grand Steward Shangqiu Cheng.

sentences.zh: 初，漢節純赤，以太子持赤節，故更為黃旄加上以相別。

translations.literal: Initially Han staffs were pure red; because the crown prince held a red staff, they therefore changed to adding yellow pennants on top to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Han staffs were pure red; because the crown prince held a red staff, they therefore added yellow pennants on top to distinguish them.

sentences.zh: 太子立車北軍南門外，召護北軍使者任安，與節，令發兵。

translations.literal: The crown prince stood by his chariot outside the south gate of the Northern Army barracks, summoned the envoy to protect the Northern Army Ren An, gave him the staff, and ordered him to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince stood by his chariot outside the south gate of the Northern Army barracks, summoned the envoy to protect the Northern Army Ren An, gave him the staff, and ordered him to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 安拜受節；

translations.literal: An bowed and received the staff;
translations.idiomatic: An bowed and received the staff;

sentences.zh: 入，閉門不出。

translations.literal: entered, closed the gate, and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: he entered, closed the gate, and did not come out.

sentences.zh: 太子引兵去，驅四市人凡數萬眾，至長樂西闕下，逢丞相軍，合戰五日，死者數萬人，血流入溝中。

translations.literal: The crown prince led troops away, drove men from the four markets totaling tens of thousands, to below the western tower of Changle, met the Chancellor's army, and fought together five days; the dead were tens of thousands, and blood flowed into the ditches.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince led troops away, drove men from the four markets totaling tens of thousands to below the western tower of Changle, met the Chancellor's army, and fought for five days; tens of thousands died, and blood flowed into the ditches.

sentences.zh: 民間皆云太子反，以故眾不附太子，丞相附兵浸多。

translations.literal: Among the people all said the crown prince had rebelled; for this reason the masses did not attach to the crown prince, while the Chancellor's attached troops gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people all said the crown prince had rebelled; for this reason the masses did not rally to the crown prince, while the Chancellor's attached troops gradually increased.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，太子兵敗，南奔覆盎城門。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the crown prince's army was defeated and fled south to Fuchang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the crown prince's army was defeated and fled south to Fuchang Gate.

sentences.zh: 司直田仁部閉城門，以為太子父子之親，不欲急之，太子由是得出亡。

translations.literal: Director of Integrity Tian Ren's unit closed the city gate, thinking that as father and son the crown prince was kin and not wishing to press him hard; the crown prince thereby got out and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Integrity Tian Ren's unit closed the city gate, thinking that as father and son the crown prince was kin and not wishing to press him hard; the crown prince thereby escaped.

sentences.zh: 丞相欲斬仁，御史大夫暴勝之謂丞相曰：「司直，吏二千石，當先請，奈何擅斬之！

translations.literal: The Chancellor wished to execute Ren; Grand Counsellor Bao Shengzhi said to the Chancellor: "Director of Integrity is an official of two thousand bushels—one should first request permission; how can you execute him on your own authority!
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor wished to execute Ren; Grand Counsellor Bao Shengzhi said to the Chancellor, "Director of Integrity is an official of two thousand bushels—one should first request permission; how can you execute him on your own authority!

sentences.zh: 」丞相釋仁。

translations.literal: " The Chancellor released Ren.
translations.idiomatic: " The Chancellor released Ren.

sentences.zh: 上聞而大怒，下吏責問御史大夫曰：「司直縱反者，丞相斬之，法也；

translations.literal: The emperor heard it and was greatly angry; he sent officials down to rebuke and interrogate the Grand Counsellor, saying: "Director of Integrity indulged rebels—the Chancellor executed him; that is the law;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard it and was greatly angry; he sent officials down to rebuke and interrogate the Grand Counsellor, saying, "Director of Integrity indulged rebels—the Chancellor executed him; that is the law;

sentences.zh: 大夫何以擅止之？

translations.literal: why did you, Grand Counsellor, arbitrarily stop it?
translations.idiomatic: why did you, Grand Counsellor, arbitrarily stop it?

sentences.zh: 」勝之惶恐，自殺。

translations.literal: " Shengzhi in fear and trembling killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Shengzhi in fear and trembling killed himself.

sentences.zh: 詔遣宗正劉長、執金吾劉敢奉策收皇后璽綬，后自殺。

translations.literal: An edict sent Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Chang and Commandant of the Metropolitan Guard Liu Gan bearing a decree to receive the empress's seal and ribbon; the empress killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Chang and Commandant of the Metropolitan Guard Liu Gan bearing a decree to receive the empress's seal and ribbon; the empress killed herself.

sentences.zh: 上以為任安老吏，見兵事起，欲坐觀成敗，見勝者合從之，有兩心，與田仁皆要斬。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Ren An was an old official; when the military affair arose he wished to sit and observe success and failure, and when he saw the victor he would join with him—he had two hearts; with Tian Ren both were sentenced to decapitation at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Ren An was an old official; when the military affair arose he wished to sit and observe success and failure, and when he saw the victor he would join with him—he had divided loyalties; with Tian Ren both were sentenced to decapitation at the waist.

sentences.zh: 上以馬通獲如侯，長安男子景建從通獲石德，商丘成力戰獲張光，封通為重合侯，建為德侯，成為秺侯。

translations.literal: The emperor because Ma Tong captured Ru Hou, Chang'an man Jing Jian with Tong captured Shi De, and Shangqiu Cheng fought fiercely and captured Zhang Guang, enfeoffed Tong as Marquis of Chonghe, Jian as Marquis of De, and Cheng as Marquis of Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ma Tong captured Ru Hou, Chang'an man Jing Jian with Tong captured Shi De, and Shangqiu Cheng fought fiercely and captured Zhang Guang, the emperor enfeoffed Tong as Marquis of Chonghe, Jian as Marquis of De, and Cheng as Marquis of Zhe.

sentences.zh: 諸太子賓客嘗出入宮門，皆坐誅；

translations.literal: All the crown prince's retainers who had gone in and out of the palace gates were punished with execution;
translations.idiomatic: All the crown prince's retainers who had gone in and out of the palace gates were punished with execution;

sentences.zh: 其隨太子發兵，以反法族，吏士劫略者皆徙敦煌郡。

translations.literal: those who followed the crown prince in raising troops, by the law of rebellion had their clans exterminated; officials and soldiers who plundered were all exiled to Dunhuang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: those who followed the crown prince in raising troops, by the law of rebellion had their clans exterminated; officials and soldiers who plundered were all exiled to Dunhuang commandery.

sentences.zh: 以太子在外，始置屯兵長安諸城門。

translations.literal: Because the crown prince was outside, for the first time garrison troops were stationed at Chang'an's various city gates.
translations.idiomatic: Because the crown prince was outside, for the first time garrison troops were stationed at Chang'an's various city gates.

sentences.zh: 上怒甚，群下憂懼，不知所出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry; the multitude below were worried and fearful, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angry; the officials below were worried and fearful, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 壺關三老茂上書曰：「臣聞父者猶天，母者猶地，子猶萬物也，故天平，地安，物乃茂成；

translations.literal: Elder of Huguan Mao memorialized, saying: "Your subject has heard that the father is like Heaven, the mother like Earth, the son like the ten thousand things—thus Heaven is balanced, Earth peaceful, and things then flourish and succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Elder of Huguan Mao memorialized, saying, "Your subject has heard that the father is like Heaven, the mother like Earth, the son like the ten thousand things—thus Heaven is balanced, Earth peaceful, and things then flourish and succeed;

sentences.zh: 父慈，母愛，子乃孝順。

translations.literal: the father kind, the mother loving, the son then filial and obedient.
translations.idiomatic: the father kind, the mother loving, the son then filial and obedient.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子為漢嗣，承萬世之業，體祖宗之重，親則皇帝之宗子也。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince is Han's heir, undertakes the enterprise of ten thousand generations, bears the weight of the ancestral temples—by kinship he is the emperor's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Now the crown prince is Han's heir, undertakes the enterprise of ten thousand generations, bears the weight of the ancestral temples—by kinship he is the emperor's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 江充，布衣之人，閭閻之隸臣耳；

translations.literal: Jiang Chong is a man of common cloth, a lackey servant of lanes and alleys;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chong is a man of common cloth, a lackey servant of lanes and alleys;

sentences.zh: 陛下顯而用之，銜至尊之命以迫蹴皇太子，造飾奸詐，群邪錯繆，是以親戚之路鬲塞而不通。

translations.literal: Your Majesty prominently employed him, bearing the Most August command to press and trample the crown prince, fabricating wicked fraud; the wicked were confused and wrong—thereby the path of kin was blocked and not open.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty prominently employed him, bearing the Most August command to press and trample the crown prince, fabricating wicked fraud; the wicked were confused and wrong—thereby the path of kin was blocked and not open.

sentences.zh: 太子進則不得見上，退則困於亂臣，獨冤結而無告，不忍忿忿之心，起而殺充，恐懼逋逃，子盜父兵，以救難自免耳。

translations.literal: The crown prince advancing could not see the emperor; retreating was trapped by disorderly ministers, alone wronged with no one to tell, unable to bear an angry heart—he rose and killed Chong, feared and fled; a son stole his father's troops to save calamity and exempt himself.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince advancing could not see the emperor; retreating he was trapped by disorderly ministers, alone wronged with no one to tell, unable to bear an angry heart—he rose and killed Chong, feared and fled; a son stole his father's troops to save himself from calamity.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為無邪心。

translations.literal: Your subject privately thinks he had no rebellious heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject privately thinks he had no rebellious heart.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：『營營青蠅，止於籓。

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'Buzzing green flies, stop at the fence.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, 'Buzzing green flies, stop at the fence.

sentences.zh: 愷悌君子，無信讒言。

translations.literal: Harmonious, gentle gentleman—do not trust slanderous words.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious, gentle gentleman—do not trust slanderous words.

sentences.zh: 讒言罔極，交亂四國。

translations.literal: Slander reaches the limit, confuses and disorders the four states.
translations.idiomatic: Slander reaches the limit, confuses and disorders the four states.

sentences.zh: 』往者江充讒殺趙太子，天下莫不聞。

translations.literal: ' Formerly Jiang Chong by slander killed the Zhao crown prince—all under Heaven has heard it.
translations.idiomatic: ' Formerly Jiang Chong by slander killed the Zhao crown prince—all under Heaven has heard it.

sentences.zh: 陛下不省察，深過太子，發盛怒，舉大兵而求之，三公自將。

translations.literal: Your Majesty did not examine and investigate, deeply faulted the crown prince, sent forth great wrath, raised a great army to seek him, and the Three Excellencies led troops themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty did not examine and investigate, deeply faulted the crown prince, sent forth great wrath, raised a great army to seek him, and the Three Excellencies led troops themselves.

sentences.zh: 智者不敢言，辯士不敢說，臣竊痛之！

translations.literal: The wise dared not speak, debaters dared not argue—your subject privately grieves it!
translations.idiomatic: The wise dared not speak, debaters dared not argue—your subject privately grieves it!

sentences.zh: 唯陛下寬心慰意，少察所親，毋患太子之非，亟罷甲兵，無令太子久亡！

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty broaden your heart and comfort your intent, slightly examine those close to you, do not worry over the crown prince's wrong, urgently halt armor and troops, and do not let the crown prince long remain a fugitive!
translations.idiomatic: Only may Your Majesty broaden your heart and comfort your intent, slightly examine those close to you, do not worry over the crown prince's wrong, urgently halt armor and troops, and do not let the crown prince long remain a fugitive!

sentences.zh: 臣不勝惓惓，出一旦之命，待罪建章宮下！

translations.literal: Your subject cannot bear earnest care, offers at once life's command, and awaits punishment below Jianzhang Palace!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject cannot bear earnest care, offers at once his life's command, and awaits punishment below Jianzhang Palace!

sentences.zh: 」書奏，天子感寤，然尚未顯言赦之也。

translations.literal: " The memorial was presented; the Son of Heaven was moved and awakened, yet still did not openly say to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was presented; the Son of Heaven was moved and awakened, yet still did not openly say to pardon him.

sentences.zh: 太子亡，東至湖，藏匿泉鳩里；

translations.literal: The crown prince fled, east to Hu, and hid at Quanjiu li;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince fled east to Hu and hid at Quanjiu li;

sentences.zh: 主人家貧，常賣屨以給太子。

translations.literal: the host family was poor and often sold sandals to supply the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: the host family was poor and often sold sandals to supply the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子有故人在湖，聞其富贍，使人呼之而發覺。

translations.literal: The crown prince had an old acquaintance in Hu; hearing he was wealthy, he sent someone to summon him and was discovered.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had an old acquaintance in Hu; hearing he was wealthy, he sent someone to summon him and was discovered.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛亥，吏圍捕太子。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinhai, officials surrounded and captured the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinhai, officials surrounded and captured the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子自度不得脫，即入室距戶自經。

translations.literal: The crown prince estimated he could not escape, then entered the room, barred the door, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince estimated he could not escape, then entered the room, barred the door, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 山陽男子張富昌為卒，足蹋開戶，新安令史李壽趨抱解太子。

translations.literal: Shanyang man Zhang Fuchang as a soldier kicked open the door with his foot; Xin'an order-clerk Li Shou rushed to embrace and undo the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang man Zhang Fuchang as a soldier kicked open the door with his foot; Xin'an order-clerk Li Shou rushed to embrace and undo the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 主人公遂格鬥死，皇孫二人皆並遇害。

translations.literal: The host thereupon fought and died; the two imperial grandsons both together met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The host thereupon fought and died; the two imperial grandsons both met calamity together.

sentences.zh: 上既傷太子，乃封李壽為邘侯，張富昌為題侯。

translations.literal: The emperor, having grieved the crown prince, then enfeoffed Li Shou as Marquis of Yu and Zhang Fuchang as Marquis of Ti.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having grieved the crown prince, then enfeoffed Li Shou as Marquis of Yu and Zhang Fuchang as Marquis of Ti.

sentences.zh: 初，上為太子立博望苑，使通賓客，從其所好，故賓客多以異端進者。

translations.literal: Initially the emperor for the crown prince established Bowang Park, allowed guests to come and go, and let him follow his preferences—therefore many retainers entered by heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the emperor for the crown prince established Bowang Park, allowed guests to come and go, and let him follow his preferences—therefore many retainers entered by heterodox ways.

sentences.zh: :臣光曰：古之明王教養太子，為之擇方正敦良之士，以為保傅、師友，使朝夕與之遊處。

translations.literal: : Your subject Guang says: Ancient enlightened kings in educating and nurturing the crown prince chose upright and honest worthy scholars for him as protectors, tutors, and friends, and made them morning and evening associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: : Your subject Guang says: Ancient enlightened kings in educating and nurturing the crown prince chose upright and honest worthy scholars for him as protectors, tutors, and friends, and made them morning and evening associate with him.

sentences.zh: 左右前後無非正人，出入起居無非正道，然猶有淫放邪僻而陷於禍敗者焉，今乃使太子自通賓客，從其所好。

translations.literal: Left, right, before, behind—none were not upright men; going out and in, rising and resting—none were not upright paths—yet still there were those who indulged in dissipation and fell into disaster; now they let the crown prince himself receive guests and follow his likes.
translations.idiomatic: Left, right, before, behind—none were not upright men; going out and in, rising and resting—none were not upright paths—yet still there were those who indulged in dissipation and fell into disaster; now they let the crown prince himself receive guests and follow his likes.

sentences.zh: 夫正直難親，諂諛易合，此固中人之常情，宜太子之不終也！

translations.literal: Uprightness is hard to be close to; flattery is easy to join—this is indeed the common feeling of mediocre men—no wonder the crown prince did not end well!
translations.idiomatic: Uprightness is hard to be close to; flattery is easy to join—this is indeed the common feeling of mediocre men—no wonder the crown prince did not end well!

translations.literal: ---- 6 On guihai, an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 6 On guihai, there was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: ---- 7 九月，商丘成為御史大夫。

translations.literal: ---- 7 In the ninth month, Shangqiu Cheng was made Grand Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 7 In the ninth month, Shangqiu Cheng was appointed Grand Counsellor.

sentences.zh: ---- 8 立趙敬肅王小子偃為平干王。

translations.literal: ---- 8 The Zhao King Jing Su's young son Yan was established as King of Pinggan.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 8 The Zhao King Jing Su's young son Yan was established as King of Pinggan.

sentences.zh: ---- 9 匈奴入上谷，五原，殺掠吏民。

translations.literal: ---- 9 The Xiongnu entered Shanggu and Wuyuan, killing and plundering officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 9 The Xiongnu entered Shanggu and Wuyuan, killing and plundering officials and people.

sentences.zh: 征和三年（辛卯，公元前九零年） 1 春，正月，上行幸雍，至安定、北地。

translations.literal: 3rd year of Zhenghe (ximao, 90 BCE) 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled in person to Yong, reaching Anding and Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: 3rd year of Zhenghe (ximao, 90 BCE) 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled in person to Yong, reaching Anding and Beidi.

sentences.zh: ---- 2 匈奴入五原、酒泉，殺兩都尉。

translations.literal: ---- 2 The Xiongnu entered Wuyuan and Jiuquan and killed two commandants.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 2 The Xiongnu entered Wuyuan and Jiuquan and killed two commandants.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣李廣利將七萬人出五原，商丘成將二萬人出西河，馬通將四萬騎出酒泉，擊匈奴。

translations.literal: In the third month, he sent Li Guangli leading seventy thousand men out from Wuyuan, Shangqiu Cheng leading twenty thousand out from Xihe, and Ma Tong leading forty thousand horsemen out from Jiuquan to strike the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, he sent Li Guangli leading seventy thousand men out from Wuyuan, Shangqiu Cheng leading twenty thousand out from Xihe, and Ma Tong leading forty thousand horsemen out from Jiuquan to strike the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: ---- 3 夏，五月，赦天下。

translations.literal: ---- 3 In summer, the fifth month, amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 3 In summer, the fifth month, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ---- 4 匈奴單于聞漢兵大出，悉徙其輜重北邸郅居水；

translations.literal: ---- 4 The Xiongnu Chanyu heard Han troops had come out in force and wholly moved his baggage north to lodge at Zhi Ju River;
translations.idiomatic: ---- 4 The Xiongnu Chanyu heard Han troops had come out in force and wholly moved his baggage north to lodge at Zhi Ju River;

sentences.zh: 左賢王驅其人民度余吾水六七百里，居兜銜山；

translations.literal: the Wise King of the Left drove his people across Yu Yuw River six or seven hundred li and dwelt at Douyan Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: the Wise King of the Left drove his people across Yu Yuw River six or seven hundred li and dwelt at Douyan Mountain;

sentences.zh: 單于自將精兵渡姑且水。

translations.literal: the Chanyu himself led picked troops across Guchu River.
translations.idiomatic: the Chanyu himself led picked troops across Guchu River.

sentences.zh: 商丘成軍至，追邪徑，無所見，還。

translations.literal: Shangqiu Cheng's army arrived, pursued by deviant paths, saw nothing, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shangqiu Cheng's army arrived, pursued by deviant paths, saw nothing, and returned.

sentences.zh: 匈奴使大將與李陵將三萬餘騎追漢軍，轉戰九日，至蒲奴水；

translations.literal: The Xiongnu sent a grand general with Li Ling leading more than thirty thousand horsemen to pursue the Han army; they fought in turns nine days, reaching Punu River;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu sent a grand general with Li Ling leading more than thirty thousand horsemen to pursue the Han army; they fought in turns for nine days, reaching Punu River;

sentences.zh: 虜不利，還去。

translations.literal: the enemy was not advantaged and returned and left.
translations.idiomatic: the enemy was not advantaged and returned and left.

sentences.zh: 馬通軍至天山，匈奴使大將偃渠將二萬餘騎要漢兵，見漢兵強，引去；

translations.literal: Ma Tong's army reached Tianshan; the Xiongnu sent Grand General Yan Qu leading more than twenty thousand horsemen to intercept Han troops; seeing Han troops were strong, he led away;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Tong's army reached Tianshan; the Xiongnu sent Grand General Yan Qu leading more than twenty thousand horsemen to intercept Han troops; seeing Han troops were strong, he led away;

sentences.zh: 通無所得失。

translations.literal: Tong had no gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had no gain or loss.

sentences.zh: 是時，漢恐車師遮馬通軍，遣開陵侯成娩將樓蘭、尉犁、危須等六國兵共圍車師，盡得其王民眾而還。

translations.literal: At this time Han feared Cheshi would block Ma Tong's army; it sent Marquis of Kailing Cheng Wan leading troops of Loulan, Weili, Weixu, and six states together to surround Cheshi, wholly obtained their king, people, and masses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Han feared Cheshi would block Ma Tong's army; it sent Marquis of Kailing Cheng Wan leading troops of Loulan, Weili, Weixu, and six states together to surround Cheshi, wholly obtained their king, people, and masses, and returned.

sentences.zh: 貳師將軍出塞，匈奴使右大都尉與衛律將五千騎要擊漢軍於夫羊句山峽，貳師擊破之，乘勝追北至范夫人城。

translations.literal: The Ershi general left the pass; the Xiongnu sent Right Grand Commandant with Wei Lü leading five thousand horsemen to intercept and strike the Han army at Fuyang Gou Mountain pass; the Ershi defeated them and, taking victory, pursued north to Fan Furen city.
translations.idiomatic: The Ershi general left the pass; the Xiongnu sent Right Grand Commandant with Wei Lü leading five thousand horsemen to intercept and strike the Han army at Fuyang Gou Mountain pass; the Ershi defeated them and, taking victory, pursued north to Fan Furen city.

sentences.zh: 匈奴奔走，莫敢距敵。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu fled in panic; none dared resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu fled in panic; none dared resist the enemy.

sentences.zh: 初，貳師之出也，丞相劉屈氂為祖道，送至渭橋。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Ershi went out, Chancellor Liu Quji performed the road-leaving rite and sent him to Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when the Ershi went out, Chancellor Liu Quji performed the road-leaving rite and sent him to Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 廣利曰：「願君侯早請昌邑王為太子；

translations.literal: Guangli said: "I wish you, Lord Marquis, would early request the King of Changyi as crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: Guangli said, "I wish you, Lord Marquis, would early request the King of Changyi as crown prince;

sentences.zh: 如立為帝，君侯長何憂乎！

translations.literal: if he is established as emperor, Lord Marquis long—what worry!
translations.idiomatic: if he is established as emperor, Lord Marquis—what long worry!

sentences.zh: 」屈氂許諾。

translations.literal: " Quji promised.
translations.idiomatic: " Quji promised.

sentences.zh: 昌邑王者，貳師將軍女弟李夫人子也；

translations.literal: The King of Changyi was the Ershi general's younger sister Lady Li's son;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Changyi was the Ershi general's younger sister Lady Li's son;

sentences.zh: 貳師女為屈氂子妻，故共欲立焉。

translations.literal: the Ershi's daughter was Quji's son's wife—therefore together they wished to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: the Ershi's daughter was Quji's son's wife—therefore together they wished to establish him.

sentences.zh: 會內者令郭穰告「丞相夫人祝詛上及與貳師共禱祠，欲令昌邑王為帝」，按驗，罪至大逆不道。

translations.literal: It happened the Inner Palace Clerk Guo Rang reported "the Chancellor's wife cursed the emperor and together with the Ershi prayed at shrines, wishing to make the King of Changyi emperor"—investigated, the offense reached great impiety and disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: It happened the Inner Palace Clerk Guo Rang reported "the Chancellor's wife cursed the emperor and together with the Ershi prayed at shrines, wishing to make the King of Changyi emperor"—investigated, the offense reached great impiety and disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔載屈氂廚車以徇，要斬東市，妻子梟首華陽街；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict carried Quji in the kitchen cart to display him, decapitated him at the waist in the eastern market, and his wife and children had their heads displayed on Huayang Street;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, an edict carried Quji in the kitchen cart to display him, decapitated him at the waist in the eastern market, and his wife and children had their heads displayed on Huayang Street;

sentences.zh: 貳師妻子亦收。

translations.literal: the Ershi's wife and children were also arrested.
translations.idiomatic: the Ershi's wife and children were also arrested.

sentences.zh: 貳師聞之，憂懼，其掾胡亞夫亦避罪從軍，說貳師曰：「夫人、室家皆在吏，若還，不稱意，適與獄會，郅居以北，可復得見乎！

translations.literal: The Ershi heard it and was worried and afraid; his aide Hu Yafu, also avoiding offense by following the army, advised the Ershi: "Wife and household are all in officials' hands—if you return, not to one's liking, you will just meet with prison—north of Zhi Ju, can you again be seen!
translations.idiomatic: The Ershi heard it and was worried and afraid; his aide Hu Yafu, also avoiding offense by following the army, advised the Ershi, "Wife and household are all in officials' hands—if you return, not to one's liking, you will just meet with prison—north of Zhi Ju, can you again be seen!

sentences.zh: 」貳師由是狐疑，深入要功，遂北至郅居水上。

translations.literal: " The Ershi thereby hesitated, advanced deep to seek merit, and thereupon north to Zhi Ju waters.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ershi thereby hesitated, advanced deep to seek merit, and thereupon north to Zhi Ju waters.

sentences.zh: 虜已去，貳師遣護軍將二萬騎度郅居之水，逢左賢王、左大將將二萬騎，與漢軍合戰一日，漢軍殺左大將，虜死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: The enemy had already departed; the Ershi sent Protector of the Army with twenty thousand horsemen across Zhi Ju waters, met the Wise King of the Left and Left Grand General with twenty thousand horsemen, joined battle one day with the Han army—the Han army killed the Left Grand General, and the enemy dead and wounded were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already departed; the Ershi sent Protector of the Army with twenty thousand horsemen across Zhi Ju waters, met the Wise King of the Left and Left Grand General with twenty thousand horsemen, joined battle one day with the Han army—the Han army killed the Left Grand General, and the enemy dead and wounded were very many.

sentences.zh: 軍長史與決眭都尉輝渠侯謀曰：「將軍懷異心，欲危眾求功，恐必敗。

translations.literal: Army Chief Clerk together with Colonel of Resolve Wei Qu, Marquis Hui Qu, deliberated, saying: "The general harbors a different heart, wishes to endanger the host and seek merit—fearing he will certainly be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Army Chief Clerk together with Colonel of Resolve Wei Qu, Marquis Hui Qu, deliberated, saying, "The general harbors a different heart, wishes to endanger the host and seek merit—fearing he will certainly be defeated.

sentences.zh: 」謀共執貳師。

translations.literal: " They plotted together to seize the Ershi.
translations.idiomatic: " They plotted together to seize the Ershi.

sentences.zh: 貳師聞之，斬長史，引兵還至燕然山。

translations.literal: The Ershi heard it, beheaded the Chief Clerk, and led troops back to Mount Yanran.
translations.idiomatic: The Ershi heard it, beheaded the Chief Clerk, and led troops back to Mount Yanran.

sentences.zh: 單于知漢軍勞倦，自將五萬騎遮擊貳師，相殺傷甚眾；

translations.literal: The Chanyu knew the Han army was weary and exhausted, himself led fifty thousand horsemen to intercept and strike the Ershi, and mutual killing and wounding were very many;
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu knew the Han army was weary and exhausted, himself led fifty thousand horsemen to intercept and strike the Ershi, and mutual killing and wounding were very many;

sentences.zh: 夜，塹漢軍前，深數尺，從後急擊之，軍大亂；

translations.literal: at night he trenched before the Han army several chi deep and from behind urgently struck them—the army was greatly disordered;
translations.idiomatic: at night he trenched before the Han army several chi deep and from behind urgently struck them—the army was greatly disordered;

sentences.zh: 貳師遂降。

translations.literal: the Ershi thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: the Ershi thereupon surrendered.

sentences.zh: 單于素知其漢大將，以女妻之，尊寵在衛律上。

translations.literal: The Chanyu always knew he was a great Han general, gave him his daughter in marriage, and honor and favor were above Wei Lü.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu always knew he was a great Han general, gave him his daughter in marriage, and honor and favor were above Wei Lü.

sentences.zh: 宗族遂滅。

translations.literal: The clan was thereupon extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The clan was thereupon extinguished.

translations.idiomatic: ---- 5 In autumn, there were locusts.

sentences.zh: ---- 6 九月，故城父令公孫勇與客胡倩等謀反，倩詐稱光祿大夫，言使督盜賊；

translations.literal: ---- 6 In the ninth month, former Chengyang Magistrate Gongsun Yong with client Hu Qian and others plotted rebellion; Qian falsely claimed to be Palace Attendant, saying he was sent to supervise bandits;
translations.idiomatic: ---- 6 In the ninth month, former Chengyang Magistrate Gongsun Yong with client Hu Qian and others plotted rebellion; Qian falsely claimed to be Palace Attendant, saying he was sent to supervise bandits;

sentences.zh: 淮陽太守田廣明覺知，發兵捕斬焉。

translations.literal: Huaiyang Administrator Tian Guangming detected it and sent troops to capture and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyang Administrator Tian Guangming detected it and sent troops to capture and behead them.

sentences.zh: 公孫勇衣繡衣、乘駟馬車至圉；

translations.literal: Gongsun Yong wore embroidered robes and rode a four-horse carriage to the stable park;
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yong wore embroidered robes and rode a four-horse carriage to the stable park;

sentences.zh: 圉守尉魏不害等誅之。

translations.literal: the stable park Commandant Wei Buhai and others executed him.
translations.idiomatic: the stable park Commandant Wei Buhai and others executed him.

sentences.zh: 封不害等四人為侯。

translations.literal: Buhai and four others were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Buhai and four others were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: ---- 7 吏民以巫蠱相告言者，案驗多不實。

translations.literal: ---- 7 Officials and people who reported one another for witchcraft—investigation mostly found them untrue.
translations.idiomatic: ---- 7 Officials and people who reported one another for witchcraft—investigation mostly found them untrue.

sentences.zh: 上頗知太子惶恐無它意，會高寢郎田千秋上急變，訟太子冤曰：「子弄父兵，罪當笞。

translations.literal: The emperor quite knew the crown prince was fearful with no other intent; it happened Bedchamber Attendant Tian Qianqiu urgently reported a change, pleading the crown prince's wrong, saying: "A son played with his father's troops—the offense should be caning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quite knew the crown prince was fearful with no other intent; it happened Bedchamber Attendant Tian Qianqiu urgently reported a change, pleading the crown prince's wrong, saying, "A son played with his father's troops—the offense should be caning.

sentences.zh: 天子之子過誤殺人，當何罪哉！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's son in excess fault killed a man—what offense should it be!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's son in excess fault killed a man—what offense should it be!

sentences.zh: 臣嘗夢一白頭翁教臣言。

translations.literal: Your subject once dreamed a white-haired old man taught your subject to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject once dreamed a white-haired old man taught your subject to speak.

sentences.zh: 」上乃大感寤，召見千秋，謂曰：「父子之間，人所難言也，公獨明其不然。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon was greatly moved and awakened, summoned Qianqiu, and said: "Between father and son, what men find hard to speak of—you alone clearly see it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply moved, summoned Qianqiu, and said, "Between father and son, what men find hard to speak of—you alone clearly see it is not so.

sentences.zh: 此高廟神靈使公教我，公當遂為吾輔佐。

translations.literal: This spirit of the High Temple made you teach me; you should proceed to be my aide and support.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of the High Temple sent you to teach me; you shall be my chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」立拜千秋為大鴻臚，而族滅江充家，焚蘇文於橫橋上，及泉鳩裡加兵刃於太子者，初為北地太守，後族。

translations.literal: " He immediately appointed Qianqiu as Grand Herald; exterminated Jiang Chong's clan by degrees; burned Su Wen on Heng Bridge; and those who at Quanjiu Li added weapons against the heir apparent—first Northland governor, later clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately appointed Qianqiu Grand Herald; exterminated Jiang Chong's clan; burned Su Wen on Heng Bridge; and those who had armed themselves against the heir at Quanjiu Li—first the Northland governor, later their clans were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 上憐太子無辜，乃作思子宮，為歸來望思之台於湖，天下聞而悲之。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied the heir was innocent; he thereupon built the Palace of Longing for the Son and made the Platform of Return to Look and Long at the lake; all under Heaven heard and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying the heir's innocence, the emperor built the Palace of Longing for the Son and the Platform of Return to Look and Long at the lake; all under Heaven heard and grieved.

sentences.zh: ---- 征和四年（壬辰，公元前八九年） 1 春，正月，上行幸東萊，臨大海，欲浮海求神山。

translations.literal: ---- Zhenghe year 4 (renchen, 89 BCE) 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled in favor to Donglai, approached the great sea, and wished to float on the sea seeking divine mountains.
translations.idiomatic: ---- Zhenghe year 4 (renchen, 89 BCE) 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled to Donglai, approached the sea, and wished to sail in search of the divine mountains.

sentences.zh: 群臣諫，上弗聽；

translations.literal: The ministers remonstrated; the emperor would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: The ministers remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen;

sentences.zh: 而大風晦冥，海水沸湧。

translations.literal: but great wind was dark and obscure, and the sea water boiled and surged.

sentences.zh: 然秦以之亡，漢以之興者，孝武能尊先王之道，知所統守，受忠直之言，惡人欺蔽，好賢不倦，誅賞嚴明，晚而改過，顧托得人，此其所以有亡秦之失而免亡秦之禍乎！

translations.literal: Yet Qin through this perished and Han through this rose because Emperor Xiao Wu was able to honor the Former Kings' Way, know what to uphold and guard, accept loyal and straight words, hate men who deceived and covered, love the worthy without weariness, punish and reward with strict clarity, late in life reform faults, and in entrusting care obtain the right men—this is why he had Qin's faults yet escaped Qin's calamity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qin through this perished and Han through this rose because Emperor Wu was able to honor the way of the former kings, know what to uphold, accept loyal and straight counsel, hate deception, love the worthy without weariness, punish and reward with strict clarity, reform late in life, and in entrusting care obtain the right men—this is why he had Qin's faults yet escaped Qin's calamity!

sentences.zh: 帝姊鄂邑公主共養省中，霍光、金日磾、上官桀共領尚書事。

translations.literal: The emperor's elder sister the Princess of Eyi jointly nourished him within the inner palace; Huo Guang, Jin Midi, and Shangguan Jie jointly headed Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's elder sister the Princess of Eyi jointly raised him within the inner palace; Huo Guang, Jin Midi, and Shangguan Jie jointly headed Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 光輔幼主，政自己出，天下想聞其風采。

translations.literal: Guang assisted the young ruler; government issued from himself; all under Heaven longed to hear his manner and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Guang assisted the young ruler; government issued from himself; all under Heaven longed to hear his manner and bearing.

sentences.zh: 殿中嘗有怪，一夜，群臣相驚，光召尚符璽郎，欲收取璽。

translations.literal: Once there was a marvel in the hall; one night the host of ministers were startled together; Guang summoned the gentleman of the Office of Tallies and Seals and wished to take and secure the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Once there was a marvel in the hall; one night the ministers were startled together; Guang summoned the gentleman of the Office of Tallies and Seals and wished to take and secure the seal.

sentences.zh: 郎不肯授，光欲奪之。

translations.literal: The gentleman would not hand it over; Guang wished to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman would not hand it over; Guang wished to seize it.

sentences.zh: 郎按劍曰：「臣頭可得，璽不可得也！

translations.literal: The gentleman grasped his sword and said: "Your servant's head can be obtained—the seal cannot be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman grasped his sword and said, "Your servant's head can be taken—the seal cannot be taken!

sentences.zh: 」光甚誼之。

sentences.zh: 明日，詔增此郎秩二等。

translations.literal: The next day, an edict increased this gentleman's rank by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict increased this gentleman's rank by two grades.

sentences.zh: 眾庶莫不多光。

translations.literal: The common multitude none did not admire Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The common people all admired Guang.
